findings.title: Cleanup registered for the literal alias "alias", not the IDPs the test creates
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` (also line 425) targets an IDP named "alias", which this test never creates. The 21 IDPs `idp-alias-0..20` are never removed by cleanup, so they can leak into later tests that share the realm (this changes `getForLogin` results and the counts the test asserts). The same pattern already exists at line 303, so it was probably copied. Use `"idp-alias-" + i` (and `"idp-alias-20"` at line 425). Capture the alias in a local first, because the method reference binds the `get(...)` argument immediately.

findings.title: remove() now always queries the delegate, even when the IDP is in the cache
findings.body: Before this change, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` ran only in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch. It now runs on every `remove`, before the branch, so the cached path (line 105) pays an extra DB lookup it did not need. The stored IDP is only needed for the login-invalidation check on line 111. You could take it from `cached.getIdentityProvider()` in the cached branch, and call the delegate only in the other branch. This is a minor cost, because removals are rare.

findings.title: Cache-hit path of getForLogin is not tested for org enable/disable or IDP deletion
findings.body: The cached set holds only IDP ids. The enabled state of an org-bound IDP is evaluated lazily by `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. The cache-hit path therefore relies on the callers re-checking `isEnabled()`, which `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` now does at lines 75 and 80. The new test covers only create, remove and update of IDPs. It does not cover disabling an organization while the login cache is warm, which is the scenario the bean's re-check comment describes. It also does not cover the `idp == null` fallback at line 247. A test that disables the org and then calls `getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL)` through the bean would pin this behaviour.

contracts.action: Cached getForLogin(mode, organizationId) in the Infinispan IDP storage provider
contracts.equivalent_path: getByOrganization in the same class (lines 168-211) caches IDP id sets in an IdentityProviderListQuery keyed by realm/org and fetches each model through getById.
contracts.before_after: getByOrganization also treats the org id as invalid (`isInvalid(orgId)`). getForLogin does not and checks only its own key. This is acceptable because an org-bound IDP's login availability changes only via IDP create/update/remove, all of which go through session.identityProviders().update (JpaOrganizationProvider.java:342,371; OrganizationAdapter.java:198). Org enable/disable is handled by re-checking isEnabled in the bean.
contracts.visible_effect: Login page IDP lists come from cached id sets and are resolved with getById. Wrapped models re-evaluate org enabled state, and the bean filters on it.
contracts.failure_mode: If a cached id no longer resolves, `registerInvalidation(cacheKey)` is called and the delegate result is returned, so the failure is self-healing. Updates that keep the login status unchanged leave the cache in place, and getById returns fresh data.

contracts.action: getLoginPredicate() now also requires an org-linked IDP to have BROKER_PUBLIC=true
contracts.equivalent_path: The default getForLogin (lines 165-184) already adds BROKER_PUBLIC=true to the search options for ORG_ONLY/ALL, so the predicate now matches the query.
contracts.before_after: Before this change, the predicate did not check the public flag. IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate (line 226) uses it for federated IDPs, and the org-aware subclass adds its own org filter. The extra clause is redundant there and consistent with it.
contracts.visible_effect: The Infinispan invalidation helpers treat a non-public org IDP as not a login IDP, so toggling it does not flush the login caches.

summary: The login-IDP cache design is sound. I found no bugs in the production code. Invalidation covers create, remove and update, including org-link changes, and every org-link change goes through `session.identityProviders().update`. The bean's `isEnabled` re-check handles org enable state on the cache-hit path. Three minor points remain. The test registers cleanup for the literal alias \"alias\", so the IDPs it creates leak (the same pattern already exists at line 303). `remove()` now always queries the delegate. There is no test for org disable with a warm login cache.
